title: Television
tipVi: Hãy phân biệt rõ giữa truyền hình truyền thống (linear television) và các nền tảng xem phim trực tuyến (streaming services) để thể hiện tư duy cập nhật và vốn từ vựng phong phú.
part1: How often do you watch television programs?
What kind of TV shows do you enjoy watching the most?
Do you prefer watching television alone or with other people?

part2.prompt: Describe an educational television program you enjoy watching
bullets: when and where you usually watch it
what topic or subject it covers
and explain why you find this program beneficial or engaging

part3: How has the way people consume television content changed over recent decades?
To what extent should governments regulate educational versus entertainment content on public television?

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu tên chương trình giáo dục mà bạn yêu thích (ví dụ: Planet Earth của BBC) và ấn tượng đầu tiên.
Ý 1: Nêu rõ hoàn cảnh bạn xem chương trình (cuối tuần, xem trên Smart TV tại phòng khách, thường xem lại qua ứng dụng).
Ý 2: Miêu tả cụ thể nội dung mà chương trình khai thác (thế giới động vật hoang dã, hệ sinh thái cực hạn, kỹ xảo quay phim chân thực).
Kết: Phân tích lý do bạn thấy chương trình bổ ích và cuốn hút (kết hợp giải trí và khoa học, nâng cao ý thức môi trường, giọng dẫn lôi cuốn).
extra.sample: I would like to talk about an exceptional educational television series called Planet Earth, produced by the BBC Natural History Unit. I usually tune in to this show on lazy Sunday evenings on my living room Smart TV, streaming it in high definition. Over time, watching an episode has become a calming ritual for me right before a demanding work week begins. The series primarily delves into wildlife biology, fragile ecosystems, and animal survival strategies across remote corners of the globe. Narrated by the legendary Sir David Attenborough, each episode captures breathtaking footage ranging from deep oceanic trenches to frozen polar tundras. What makes this program so profoundly engaging is its seamless blend of cutting-edge cinematography with scientific storytelling. Rather than bombarding the audience with dry statistics, it dramatizes natural phenomena through dramatic predator-prey chases and intimate animal behaviors. Watching it not only expands my factual understanding of biodiversity, but also awakens a genuine sense of urgency regarding environmental conservation. Ultimately, it is both intellectually stimulating and visually magnificent.

p1.q: How often do you watch television programs?
p1.a: To be honest, I rarely watch traditional broadcast TV nowadays. Instead, I stream programs a few times a week on my laptop, usually unwinding with a comedy show like Friends for half an hour before heading to bed.

p1.q: What kind of TV shows do you enjoy watching the most?
p1.a: I am particularly keen on investigative documentaries and science programs. They examine real-world issues in great depth, which I find far more intellectually rewarding than dramatic soap operas or frivolous talent competitions.

p1.q: Do you prefer watching television alone or with other people?
p1.a: I generally prefer watching solo because it allows me to pause or rewind whenever I like without negotiating with anyone. That said, when it comes to live sporting events, watching alongside enthusiastic friends is unbeatable.

p3.q: How has the way people consume television content changed over recent decades?
p3.a: In the past, viewers were constrained by strict broadcast schedules and uninterrupted commercial interruptions. Today, the rise of streaming platforms has radically personalized content consumption. People now demand on-demand access and frequently binge-watch complete seasons whenever they please. Consequently, linear television is steadily declining, particularly among digital natives who prioritize convenience and flexible viewing schedules over traditional living-room sets.

p3.q: To what extent should governments regulate educational versus entertainment content on public television?
p3.a: State authorities ought to maintain a responsible baseline by mandating minimum quotas for informative and culturally significant programming. Commercial broadcasters naturally prioritize sensationalist entertainment to maximize advertisement revenue, but public television owes a civic duty to educate the citizenry. Enforcing balanced schedules that include historical analysis and scientific discovery broadens public knowledge, preventing commercial media from reducing broadcasting purely to mindless consumerism.

mistakesVi: Lặp lại động từ 'watch TV' quá nhiều lần; nên thay thế linh hoạt bằng 'stream content', 'tune in to a broadcast', hay 'consume television programming'.
Nhầm lẫn giữa 'on TV' (phát sóng trên truyền hình) và 'on the TV' (đặt đồ vật trên bề mặt của chiếc máy thu hình).
Dùng từ 'program' để chỉ chung toàn bộ kênh truyền hình, thay vì phân biệt rõ giữa 'channel' (kênh phát sóng), 'program/show' (tập/chương trình), và 'series' (loạt phim nhiều tập).
